text:
The dynamics between Jay Gatsby and Daisy Buchanan serve as the central vehicle for exploring the novel's critique of the American Dream and the pervasive nature of illusion. Gatsby’s idealization of Daisy is not merely a romantic obsession but a projection of his desire to rewrite the past and validate his self-made identity. By treating Daisy as a symbol of status and perfection rather than a flawed human being, Gatsby embodies the theme of illusion versus reality. His relentless pursuit highlights the hollowness of materialistic values, as he believes that wealth and grand gestures can bridge the insurmountable class barriers between his new money origins and Daisy’s old money heritage. This dynamic ultimately reveals the corruption of the American Dream, showing how the pursuit of an idealized future is often rooted in a distorted and unattainable past. The tragedy of Gatsby’s downfall underscores the futility of trying to impose one’s will on reality through material means.
